name: Premium Residency -- Permanent, Annual, Special Talent, and Gifted products (Al-Iqama Al-Mumayaza)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a one-time government fee of SAR 800,000 (approx. USD 213,000) and passing financial-solvency and background checks; no investment, business, or employment is required.
requirements.fix_path: Save toward the SAR 800,000 one-time fee, or choose the Annual track if the full amount isn't available upfront.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires an annual government fee of SAR 100,000 (approx. USD 26,700), renewed each year, with the same financial-solvency and background checks as the Permanent track.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm ability to sustain the SAR 100,000/year fee; the break-even point against the Permanent track's one-time fee is around 8 years.

requirements.blocker_text: Targets skilled professionals in healthcare, science, research, and executive leadership whose knowledge and experience would benefit Saudi Arabia's development, requiring a relevant degree, professional licence, publications, or recognised achievements in the field.
requirements.fix_path: Document relevant credentials, publications, or achievements demonstrating specialised expertise.

requirements.blocker_text: One commonly-cited criterion for this specific track is a high salary threshold, around SAR 80,000+/month, materially above the SAR 14,000+ threshold associated with standard priority-sector employment -- combined with relevant degrees, licences, or achievements. This figure is cited by only one source in this research pass and could not be cross-verified against pr.gov.sa directly (see notes), so it is treated as informational rather than a confirmed hard cutoff.
requirements.fix_path: Secure or document a position meeting the high-salary threshold for this track.

requirements.blocker_text: Targets individuals with recognised achievements or active standing in culture, sports, or the arts.
requirements.fix_path: Document recognised achievements or professional standing in a qualifying cultural, sporting, or artistic field.

evidence_required.document: Proof of financial solvency (Permanent/Annual tracks) or field-specific credentials (Talent/Gifted tracks)
Medical examination and criminal-background check from country of origin
SAR 4,000 standard application fee for the category-based products (Talent, Gifted), not required for the fee-based Permanent/Annual products

outcome.duration_length: unlimited (Permanent track) or 1-5 years, renewable (Annual, Talent, Gifted tracks)
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum physical presence requirement to maintain the residency

notes: Classified as settled rather than business (unlike the Investor/Entrepreneur/Real Estate Owner tracks in sa_premium_residency_investor_entrepreneur and sa_premium_residency_real_estate) because these four products require no investment, business activity, or specific economic contribution beyond a flat fee (Permanent/Annual) or personal/professional standing (Talent/Gifted) -- the closest functional analogue in this dataset to an unconditional long-term settlement status, even though Saudi Arabia has no true 'permanent residence' status of the kind built for the other 14 countries. Same pr.gov.sa robots.txt sourcing-method limitation applies here as on the other two Premium Residency files: figures are strongly cross-corroborated across multiple independent 2026-dated sources but not directly fetched from the primary government page, flagged honestly as a follow-up target. STRUCTURAL FINDING, confirmed identically across every source checked: none of Premium Residency's products -- financial, investment, or talent-based -- lead to citizenship or accelerate the naturalisation clock in any way. This is stated as an explicit, repeated point across law-firm and relocation-consultancy sources alike ('it does not directly lead to citizenship... Naturalisation in Saudi Arabia remains a complex process'), making Premium Residency structurally closer to the UAE's Golden Visa (also citizenship-sealed) than to e.g. Portugal's or Spain's investment routes, both of which do carry a real (if slow) path to naturalisation. The Special Talent salary figure (SAR 80,000+/month) is the single thinnest-sourced numeric fact in this route -- cited by only one of the sources checked in this research pass rather than cross-corroborated across multiple independent sources the way the fee figures are -- flagged honestly here rather than presented with the same confidence as the Permanent/Annual fee amounts.
